headline: Rescue steps lift Taiwan 778 points, MediaTek limit-up; foreigners sell 6th day, still a bear-market bounce
summary: Today's big rally was built by policy, not by buyers: foreigners sold for a 6th day and added futures shorts. By the rules Taiwan is still a "bear, risk rising"; it needs to reclaim 39,858 to get back to a pullback. Tonight's US open is the first test, with QQQ 0.1% from its fourth tier on Friday. Keep regular investing on plan.

overview.lead: Taiwan's bounce was built by policy, not by returning buyers: the National Stabilization Fund and short-selling curbs 3.0 stopped the opening sell-off, and institutions kept selling.
points: The TAIEX rose 2.16% to 36,812.
It opened lower and rallied, with a 1,665-point intraday range and turnover up to NT$1.08 trillion.
MediaTek (2454), Delta (2308) and UMC (2303) hit limit-up; TSMC (2330) rose only 1.5%.
The three institutional groups still sold NT$51.2B, so institutions did not drive the bounce.
US markets open tonight; the first session after Friday's crash tests this rebound.

focus.lead: Taiwan-linked names stopped falling today and 0050 rose 3%, but fund NAVs only run to 11/19 and 11/20 and miss today's bounce.
points: 0050 rose 3.0%, narrowing its drawdown to −25.3%.
0050's fifth tier at 81.55 is now 6.3% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV on 11/20 is −43.5% from its high, the deepest of the nine.
MediaTek, a top-three name in Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8), hit limit-up; TSMC rose 1.5%.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV is still at 11/19, missing both the 11/20 plunge and today's bounce.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) NAV fell 7.1% on 11/20 to −31.2% from its high, past its fifth tier.
SPY, QQQ and AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) still reflect Friday's crash; new prices come tonight.

position.lead: By the framework, nothing new triggered in Taiwan today: 0050 moved further from its fifth tier, and AB International Technology's 11/20 NAV passed its fifth tier, using up all tiers.
points: 0050 has used 70% of the reserve over four tiers; the fifth tier is 6.3% away.
QQQ's fourth tier at 607.73 was only 0.1% away at Friday's close.
SPY's third tier is 4.0% away.
AB Select US Equity's second tier is 2.2% away (11/19 NAV).
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 7.5% from its fifth tier; Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan is 10.9% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology have used all tiers; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: No new US data today, so the macro picture is Friday's: safe-haven money is in Treasuries and credit is still calm.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.92% (11/20), down 0.21 points in a month.
The high-yield spread is 3.52% (11/19), far from the 5% alarm line.
The stabilization fund cited Taiwan's 2026 growth forecast of 11.05% and 10 straight months of red business-cycle signals.
USD/TWD is 33.03 (11/20), with the Taiwan dollar 0.66 weaker in a month; it firmed this afternoon.
The US releases its November PMI flash tonight; PCE inflation on 11/25 is the week's key data.

sentiment.lead: Four of Taiwan's capitulation signals are on, and today's rally looks like the first bounce after a washout, but foreign selling has not stopped.
points: The lit signals are oversold, margin deleveraging, breadth washout and a surge in new lows.
Only extreme foreign selling is off: 20-day net selling is NT$1.04 trillion.
Listed margin balances fell to NT$435.2B on 11/20, down 32.5% in a month.
Only 9% of Taiwan stocks are above the 200-day line, with 194 new lows.
The US Fear & Greed index at 9.7 and VIX at 35.89 are Friday's readings; they update tonight.

sectors.lead: The hardest-hit electronics led and financials lagged: last month's worst groups bounced most, a classic oversold rebound.
points: Electronic components rose 6.6% but are still down 41% in a month.
Plastics rose 7.1%, with Nan Ya Plastics (1303) at limit-up.
PCB names Gold Circuit (2368) and Elite Material (2383) hit limit-up, and memory stocks bounced hard.
Financials fell: CTBC (2891) dropped 6% and Fubon (2881) 4%.
High-priced names such as GUC (3443) and CHPT (6510) closed lower, down 4% to 6%.

taiwan.lead: The bounce was built by policy and flows have not improved: foreigners sold for a 6th day and added futures shorts.
points: Foreigners sold NT$28.9B today, their 6th straight selling session.
Six-day net selling totals NT$247.6B.
Investment trusts and dealers also sold; the three groups sold NT$51.2B combined.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures stand at 103,432 contracts, up 6,645 in five days.
The FSC's short-selling curbs 3.0 took effect today: no short sales below the prior close, and short margin raised to 150%.
The National Stabilization Fund confirmed on 11/21 that it is buying, and the exchange urged companies to buy back shares.

watch.lead: Tonight's US session is the first test: if QQQ breaks its fourth tier after Friday's crash, Taiwan's bounce will be tested tomorrow.
points: Taiwan needs to reclaim 39,858 (the −20% line) to have a shot at returning to a pullback.
0050's fifth tier at 81.55 is 6.3% away.
Dell (DELL) reports on 11/24, a test of AI server demand.
US PCE and Q3 GDP come on 11/25 (21:30 Taipei); US markets close for Thanksgiving on 11/26.
A clear drop in foreign selling would signal flows are stabilizing.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is still a "bear, risk rising" and today's bounce does not change that: it is below the −20% line with 2 systemic lights on.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 11.4% below its 200-day line after 6 closes below it, but the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: the US below its 200-day line and Taiwan's broken breadth; credit, the economy and financial conditions are still fine.
The high-yield spread is 3.52%, far from the 5% alarm line.
Capitulation signals: 4 of 5 on; only extreme foreign selling is off.
History: all 7 declines that reached this level since late 2000 fell past −20%, and 4 fell past −30%.
Only 1 was a one-month crash like this one; the sample is too small, reference only.
What would change the call: a close back above 39,858, then 5 closes above the 200-day line, returns it to a pullback.
3 or more systemic lights, or a flat 200-day line, would make it a bear trend.
By the rules the US is still "pullback, risk rising"; the S&P 500 has closed below its 200-day line 4 days running.

news.title: Wider rescue steps spark a rebound: TAIEX up 778.6 points (+2.16%) to 36,811.89, MediaTek and Delta limit-up
news.read: The bounce centered on last week's hardest-hit electronics and PCB names, while financials fell; 0050 rose 3%, now 6.3% from its fifth tier.

news.title: FSC short-selling curbs 3.0 take effect: no short sales below the prior close; short margin raised from 130% to 150%
news.read: It blunted short sellers and helped the market rally from a low open; policy can slow selling, but foreign flows are what matter.

news.title: National Stabilization Fund confirms on a weekend that it is buying; Taiwan fell 7,641.83 points (17.5%) last week
news.read: State buying usually stops a crash but does not change the trend call; by the rules Taiwan is still in a bear market.

news.title: Foreigners sell NT$28.948B, NT$247.618B over 6 sessions; all three institutional groups sell
news.read: The index rose but institutions did not return; how far the bounce runs depends on when foreign selling eases.

news.title: Exchange urges financially sound companies to consider buybacks and hold more investor briefings
news.read: Buybacks add some demand but are usually small; foreign flows remain the key.

news.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent said on 11/22 that Jensen Huang is "on the outside now"; Nvidia's leadership remains unsettled
news.read: Nvidia is a major weight in QQQ and both AB funds; until leadership and accounting questions clear, US tech stays volatile.

news.title: Short US week: Dell reports 11/24, PCE and Q3 GDP on 11/25, markets closed 11/26 for Thanksgiving
news.read: Dell is the first direct check on AI server demand and PCE sets December rate-hike odds; both affect Taiwan tech.
